summary: Default cleanup proposes Docker containers and images

delivery.outcome: A flagless `fixos cleanup` proposes Docker stopped containers alongside unused images/build cache as a safe interactive action, runnable alone via `-c docker-containers`, while running containers and all volumes stay protected.
nonGoals: No cleanup or destructive operation runs on the developer host during development or tests.
No new runtime dependency or dependency manifest change.
Docker volumes are never removed or proposed.
Running containers and in-use images are never targeted.
No automatic cleanup without the existing interactive confirmation.

architecture.decision: Reuse the existing safe-age-action channel: emit a `docker-containers` planned action when `docker system df` reports reclaimable container space, execute it through a dedicated `cleanup_docker_containers` method that runs only `docker container prune --force`, and dispatch the new cleanup kind in the CLI like the existing docker-unused kind.
interfaceChanges: new `fixos cleanup -c docker-containers` cleanup kind and a Docker stopped-containers entry in the default interactive plan
architecture.rollback: Revert the commit; the default plan returns to proposing only unused images, build cache and orphaned networks.
